action_en: Avoid letting ammonia nitrogen build up in mandarin fish water by testing it regularly and acting when it rises.
action_zh: 养殖户应避免水体氨氮积累,定期检测氨氮,升高时及时采取措施。
evidence_gap: Safe thresholds differ between papers (below 0.2 mg/L versus a derived safe total ammonia nitrogen of 1.29 mg/L), and farm-condition studies of chronic low-level exposure are lacking.
risks: Frequent water exchange or extra treatments to lower ammonia can themselves stress the fish and add cost.

basis.reason: F0457 gives consistent measured evidence that ammonia harms mandarin fish in a dose-dependent way, which supports an avoid action. F1909 gives the candidate thresholds, and F0487 describes monitoring that could detect rises. I did not set a single limit because the thresholds differ and the monitoring claims have no measured welfare outcomes.

findings.why: Measured dose-dependent mortality, oxidative stress, liver enzyme changes and reduced appetite from ammonia exposure.
Gives differing recommended or derived ammonia limits.
findings.practice_en: ammonia nitrogen control in culture water

findings.why: Describes continuous real-time monitoring of ammonia, oxygen, pH and temperature, but without measured fish outcomes.

priority.reason: Ammonia harm is measured and dose-dependent (LC50 12.91 mg/L, with stress and liver damage at lower levels), and regular testing is cheap and can be done now. Thresholds differ between papers, but the downside of acting is small.

criteria.note: lethal and chronic harm, every farm

action_en: Keep dietary carbohydrate and starch in mandarin fish feeds at about 10-13% and avoid formulating above roughly 13-16%.
action_zh: 饲料厂应将鳜鱼饲料中的碳水化合物和淀粉控制在约10-13%,避免配方超过约13-16%。
evidence_gap: Reported thresholds differ between studies (about 7-16%), and effects with different fish sizes, fat levels and water types are not settled.
risks: Going too low may cut protein sparing and growth, and one study found carbohydrate improved growth and, in saline-alkaline water, a 13% diet eased tissue damage.

basis.reason: These four findings all measured harm from high carbohydrate or starch in mandarin fish, covering liver damage, lower feed intake and anorexia, and they give similar cut-off levels. I chose them over the sugar and gelatinized starch findings because they rest on more papers and more measured results. The type is avoid for high levels only, because the safe level is not fixed and low-to-moderate levels sometimes showed no effect.

findings.why: Measured liver damage once carbohydrate passed about 7-13%
Lower intake and anorexia at high levels; best around 10-13%
Liver damage and higher AST/ALT above about 13-16% starch
High-sugar diets lowered intake and growth; only some fish became anorexic

priority.reason: Many measured papers (51 measured claims in F0535 alone) show liver damage and reduced feed intake from high carbohydrate, so capping it is a clear feed-formulation step. Thresholds vary between 7 and 16%, which keeps it just below the top.

criteria.note: liver damage and anorexia, all fed fish
slightly lower growth if too low

action_en: Keep dietary lipid in mandarin fish feeds near 12% and avoid levels of about 16% or more.
action_zh: 饲料厂应将鳜鱼饲料脂肪含量控制在约12%,避免达到约16%或更高。
evidence_gap: The safe upper limit is only bracketed between about 12% and 16%, and interactions with protein and carbohydrate are unclear.
risks: Lowering fat too far slows growth and disturbs metabolism, and higher fat raises voluntary feed intake, so a cut may reduce intake.

basis.reason: These findings agree that high dietary lipid gives fat build-up and liver injury, with measured changes at about 16% or more, while 12% gave best growth or intake without liver load. I included F0578 because it shows the intake benefit that makes higher fat tempting. None measured infection or parasites, and growth results conflict, so I limited this to avoiding high levels rather than setting an exact target.

findings.why: Measured liver and viscera lipid build-up and vacuolation at about 16% lipid
Serum AST/ALT rose and liver necrosis appeared at about 15.9-18% lipid
12% fat gave best growth; too much caused fatty liver
Intake rose with lipid; 12% gave maximal intake without liver load, 18% gave no better growth

priority.reason: Measured studies consistently link lipid of about 16% or more to fatty liver and liver injury, and about 12% gave the best growth. The safe upper limit is only bracketed, and lipid lowers intake slightly, so it ranks just under carbohydrate.

criteria.note: measured, no paper shows a benefit of high fat

action_en: Monitor survival, liver and gut condition, and non-feeding individuals during staged training of mandarin fish from live bait to formulated feed.
action_zh: 养殖户应在鳜鱼由活饵逐步驯化到配合饲料期间,监测成活率、肝肠状况和拒食个体。
evidence_gap: It is unclear what separates fish that adapt from those that refuse or develop liver and gut problems, and which training steps best protect health.
risks: Fish that fail to feed may lose condition or die, and monitoring adds labour and may not reduce losses by itself.

basis.reason: Staged training reports success from about 53% to over 90%, with gradual switching said to reduce stress, but other findings link training to pale livers, gut adaptation problems and individual variation. The mixed picture is why this is a monitoring action rather than adopting one training method. I chose these four because they cover both the benefit and the health risk, and did not use findings that only describe equipment or feed shape.

findings.why: Success rates vary from about 53% to over 90%, with relapses and individual differences
findings.practice_en: feed training (domestication) from live bait to dead bait and formulated feed
findings.practice_zh: 驯食（活饵转死饵及配合饲料驯化）

findings.why: Slow stepwise switch reduced fry stress in one measured study
findings.practice_en: gradual transition from live bait to artificial feed
findings.practice_zh: 逐步转食驯化（活饵到配合饲料）

findings.why: Pale livers measured in late-stage artificial-feed group; illness and death linked to training
Poor intestinal adaptation and higher gut disease risk after the switch

priority.reason: Staged live-bait to formulated-feed training is very widely used (75 papers, 50 measured claims), and non-feeding and liver or gut problems are real. Monitoring is cheap and low-risk, but it does not by itself reduce losses.

criteria.note: starvation and gut or liver problems
many papers, mixed on health effects

action_en: Monitor water temperature in mandarin fish culture as a disease-risk indicator, watching for viral disease risk above about 20°C and for water mould at low temperatures, without cooling so far that feeding drops.
action_zh: 养殖户应将水温监测作为鳜病害风险指标,关注约20°C以上的病毒病风险和低温下的水霉病,同时避免降温过度影响摄食。
evidence_gap: It is not known whether deliberately holding temperature lower reduces outbreaks on farms, since lower temperature may only leave fish as latent carriers.
risks: Lower temperatures were linked to latent infection, more water mould and reduced feeding and poorer condition after cooling, so temperature trade-offs may harm welfare.

basis.reason: F0431 and F0425 show measured links between temperature and viral disease outcomes but point to both benefits and harms of low temperature. F1952 shows that cooling cuts feeding and condition. Because the findings conflict, I recommend monitoring instead of setting a temperature to adopt.

findings.why: Measured ISKNV and MRV outcomes depend on temperature, with latent infection at 19°C and more water mould below 18°C.
Fewer deaths at lower temperature, but infection persisted and saprolegniasis occurred at suitable temperatures.
Measured cooling from 14.5 to 7.5°C reduced feeding and weakened immune and liver function.

priority.reason: Measured studies show disease strongly tied to temperature (ISKNV above 20°C, MRV at 26°C, water mould when cold), and cooling too far cuts feeding. Monitoring is cheap, but the evidence on temperature control is mixed.

action_en: Run controlled farm trials of inactivated ISKNV and ISKNV-based bivalent vaccines in mandarin fish, recording protection, how long it lasts, injection handling and cost.
action_zh: 研究人员应在养殖场开展对照试验，评估鳜鱼ISKNV灭活疫苗及ISKNV二价疫苗的保护效果、保护持续时间、注射操作负担和成本。
evidence_gap: Most protection figures are developers' claims or challenge results without stated conditions, and durability under farm conditions and the welfare cost of injection are not measured.
risks: Injection handling can stress fish, trained injectors and a high per-fish cost may limit uptake, and current inactivated vaccines may give limited protection duration.

basis.reason: These three findings all concern inactivated vaccines against viral disease and together show strong claimed protection alongside stated limits on efficacy, duration and cost. I left out vaccine preparation and antiviral-development findings because they only describe work and report no effect. Protection is reported but mostly not newly measured, and F0348 is mixed on limits, so a farm trial rather than adoption is the supported step.

findings.why: Reports high claimed protection for the ISKNV vaccine, with most figures coming from developers or background statements.
Gives measured challenge protection of 80-100% for bivalent vaccines, without stating conditions or doses.
Shows vaccination is widely described as effective but notes limits in efficacy, duration, injector skill and cost.

priority.reason: ISKNV is a major killer, and two measured challenge trials show over 90% protection. Most other figures are developers' claims and injection stress and cost are unmeasured, so farm trials are justified but not top priority.

action_en: Test salt-water soaking (about 3% for 5-10 minutes) of live bait fish before feeding on farms, and record disease and parasite outcomes against unsoaked bait.
action_zh: 养殖户应在养殖场试验投喂前用约3%盐水浸泡饵料鱼5-10分钟,并与未浸泡组比较记录病害和寄生虫情况。
evidence_gap: No measured change in disease or parasite rates after bait disinfection has been reported, and the best salt level and soak time are not tested.
risks: Handling and salt exposure may stress or injure bait fish, and soaking may not remove virus carried inside the bait fish.

basis.reason: Bait fish are shown as a route for pathogens such as ISKNV, and three findings agree that disinfecting or inspecting bait before feeding is the control, but they only describe the practice. I put them together because they address the same risk and cite the same salt-water method. Without measured disease results this cannot be called adopt, so it is a farm trial.

findings.why: Salt soaking (mostly about 3%, 5-10 min) described as killing parasites and bacteria; no measured disease change
findings.practice_en: salt water disinfection of bait fish before feeding
findings.practice_zh: 饵料鱼食盐水浸泡消毒

findings.why: Recommends inspecting, quarantining and disinfecting bait before feeding
findings.practice_en: bait fish inspection and disinfection before feeding

findings.why: Recommends disinfecting feeder fish; no measured effect
Shows bait fish as an infection route, including a high measured ISKNV rate

priority.reason: Bait fish are a documented disease route (20 papers; one measured ISKNV link), and salt soaking is cheap and easy. It is almost entirely a stated recommendation with no measured disease effect, so it is framed as a test.

action_en: Test whether PCR screening and quarantine of fry for ISKNV and MRV before stocking reduce later disease in mandarin fish farms, using adequate sample sizes.
action_zh: 研究人员应检验放养前对鳜鱼苗进行ISKNV和MRV的PCR筛查与检疫，在使用足够样本量的情况下能否降低后期发病。
evidence_gap: Studies report virus-free test results at stocking, but only one claim links origin quarantine to lower disease, with no numbers and no measured later disease or welfare outcomes.
risks: Too small a sample can miss latent infections such as ISKNV, giving false assurance, and testing and quarantine add cost and holding time for fry.

basis.reason: These findings all describe screening fry for viruses before they enter ponds, using PCR and quarantine, so they form one practice. I chose them over general health-check findings because they name the specific viruses and the detection method. The evidence is mostly negative test results and descriptions, with one unquantified claim of lower disease, so a trial is more appropriate than adoption.

findings.why: Shows tested fry were often free of major viruses and warns that small samples can miss detections.
findings.practice_en: pathogen testing of fry before stocking

findings.why: Supports quarantine and screening at source, including one claim of lower disease after origin quarantine in Shandong.
Explains why rapid screening is needed for latent ISKNV and MRV.
Shows PCR can confirm freedom from viruses and identify ranavirus, as a diagnostic tool only.
Describes quarantine of one to two weeks plus PCR checks before experiments.

priority.reason: Screening fry for ISKNV and MRV before stocking addresses disease at source and is widely recommended (12 papers). Evidence is negative test results rather than measured later disease, and small samples can give false reassurance.

action_en: Trial recirculating aquaculture systems against pond rearing on commercial mandarin fish farms, recording water quality, survival, drug use and gut health together.
action_zh: 养殖场应在商业养殖条件下开展循环水养殖系统与池塘养殖的对比试验,同时记录水质、成活率、用药量和肠道健康。
evidence_gap: Much of the disease-reduction wording is inferred or claimed rather than measured, and no study shows that fewer pathogenic gut bacteria lead to fewer outbreaks.
risks: A simpler gut microbial community may weaken microbial competition and immune stimulation, and connected water can spread pathogens between tanks, so the systems cost more to run and manage.

basis.reason: I grouped the recirculating-system findings because they cover the same technology and address both water quality and disease. F0507 is the strongest, with measured stable oxygen, pH, ammonia and nitrite across many papers. F0420 and F1705 are weaker on disease, so I chose a farm trial instead of adoption.

findings.why: Measured gut microbiota, survival and drug-use data suggest less disease, but with a caution about a simpler gut community.
findings.practice_zh: 工业化循环水养殖系统

findings.why: Measured stable dissolved oxygen, pH, ammonia and nitrite in recirculating systems.
Notes that connected water can spread disease unless biosecurity and prompt isolation of sick fish are in place.

priority.reason: RAS has measured stable water quality across many papers and some measured gut and survival benefits. Much of the disease wording is inferred, and the systems are costly and need new equipment.

criteria.note: 17 papers on water, thin on disease

action_en: Avoid breeding programmes that select only for feed acceptance, or that inbreed without proper selection, without monitoring disease and growth in each generation.
action_zh: 避免只以摄食人工饲料为目标、或在缺乏恰当选择下近交的育种方案;每一代都要监测发病和生长情况。
evidence_gap: It is unclear whether the poor results after five generations came from the selection method, inbreeding, or the feeding conditions, and no quantified data are given.
risks: Pausing or changing selection may delay progress towards accepting formulated feed and could raise short-term costs for breeders.

basis.reason: Both findings describe the same background report: after five generations of selection for feed acceptance, most fish still refused feed, grew slowly and fell ill, and F0002 adds two warnings about inbreeding. I chose these over the supportive stated claims because they are the only ones pointing to harm. The evidence is a mixed, unmeasured report, so I limited the action to avoiding unmonitored selection and did not call for stopping breeding.

findings.why: Reports sick, slow-growing fish after five generations, plus warnings on inbreeding
Same report: most fish still refused feed and fell ill, and no welfare benefit was measured

priority.reason: One measured study shows survival gain from selection, but a report of five generations of feed-acceptance selection gave sick, slow fish, and inbreeding warnings are consistent. The cause is unquantified and the advice is cautious and cheap.

action_en: Keep up daily pond patrols that record fish activity, feeding, body surface and water quality (dissolved oxygen, temperature, pH), and watch fry vitality in nursery stages, so problems are noticed early and logged.
action_zh: 养殖户应坚持每日巡塘，记录鱼的活动、摄食、体表和水质（溶解氧、温度、pH），并在育苗阶段观察鱼苗活力，以便及早发现并记录问题。
evidence_gap: No paper reports a measured change in disease, parasite or water-quality outcomes from patrols, and the check frequency and the triggers for action are not compared.
risks: Patrols cost labour time and only catch problems that are visible, and the fish may be disturbed or handled when checked.

basis.reason: These findings all describe the same low-tech routine of daily observation, applied to disease and to water quality, so I grouped them into one monitoring action. The authors agree that it is useful, but the claims mostly describe the practice and few measure any effect, so I classed it as monitor rather than adopt.

findings.why: Eight papers describe daily patrols to spot disease early
Daily checks of signs and mortality, with microscopy and IoT early warning, described
Patrols linked to early fixes for low oxygen and poor water
Daily activity, oxygen, temperature and pH checks described
Fry vitality observation (swimming, responsiveness, breathing) described

priority.reason: Daily patrols are cheap, universal and could catch low oxygen or disease early, but the 8+ papers only describe the practice and none measures an effect.

action_en: Test matching live bait fish length to mandarin fish body length (about one-third, within roughly 20-50%) on farms, and record swallowing failures, deaths and growth.
action_zh: 养殖户应在养殖场试验使饵料鱼体长与鳜鱼体长相匹配(约三分之一,大致20-50%),并记录吞咽失败、死亡和生长情况。
evidence_gap: Recommended size ratios range widely (about 20% to 70% of body length) and few studies measured welfare outcomes.
risks: Bait that is too small raises hunting energy and cost, and bait that is too large can cause failed swallowing or choking death.

basis.reason: These findings give similar size rules for bait fish, with about one-third often named best, and warn about choking with oversized bait. I used them rather than the pellet size and feed shape findings, which also lack measured outcomes, because bait size has a stated death risk. Most statements are recommendations with few measurements and the stated ratios differ, so this is a trial.

findings.why: Gives size ratios; oversized bait causes choking, undersized raises energy cost; few measurements
Bait shorter than half the fish's length; mostly described practice
findings.practice_en: bait size matching by growth stage
findings.practice_zh: 按生长阶段调整饵料规格

findings.why: Prey of 26-36% of body length swallowed best in adults

priority.reason: Oversized bait can cause choking deaths and undersized bait costs energy, with 19 agreeing papers. Few measured outcomes and ratios range from 20 to 70%, so a farm test is appropriate.

action_en: Test moderate water flow of about 0.4–0.7 m/s in cages to support feed training of mandarin fish on dead bait, while checking that fry are not tired by it.
action_zh: 养殖户应在网箱中试验约0.4–0.7 m/s的适度水流以促进鳜摄食死饵驯化,并检查鱼苗是否因水流而疲劳。
evidence_gap: Only one measured study gives a flow range for dead-bait feeding, and the claims on flushing and micro-flow are mostly stated rather than quantified.
risks: Flow that is too high tires fry and prevents rest and digestion after feeding, while too low causes oxygen shortage, and other papers advise low flow to save fish energy.

basis.reason: F1879 gives the only measured flow range for feeding on dead bait, and F1864 shows that many papers describe flushing water as encouraging feeding. F2110 warns that both too much and too little flow can harm fish, so a farm trial is more appropriate than adoption.

findings.why: Measured that cage flow of 0.4–0.7 m/s promoted feeding on dead bait, with too much or too little unfavourable.
Eleven papers describe flushing water as helping fish start feeding, though effects are not quantified.
Warns that flow that is too low or too high can cause oxygen shortage or exhaustion and death in fry.

priority.reason: Flushing water is widely described as helping fish start feeding on dead bait, and one measured study gives a 0.4-0.7 m/s range. Evidence is thin and flow that is too high tires fry.

action_en: Run controlled farm trials comparing selectively bred or hybrid mandarin fish with ordinary stock, recording survival, disease outbreaks and drug use under the same conditions.
action_zh: 开展对照养殖试验,在相同条件下比较选育或杂交鳜与普通鳜的存活率、疾病暴发和用药情况。
evidence_gap: Only two measured studies (a 12.6% survival gain in one population, and hybrids with no outbreaks over 6 and 7 years) exist, and there are no side-by-side trials, no conditions given, and no data showing resistance to specific pathogens such as iridovirus.
risks: Resistance claims may rest on farmer reports; a strain chosen for resistance or growth could lose other traits, and hybrids could add genetic or escape concerns the findings do not address.

basis.reason: These three findings all concern whether bred or hybrid strains reduce disease, and they are the ones with some measured results (F0002, F0635) or consistent support (F0626). They are grouped as a trial because the support is mostly stated or farmer-reported, F0002 is mixed, and most claims give no conditions, so adoption is not justified.

findings.why: Measured 12.6% survival gain in one population, but also warns of poor results and inbreeding
Three papers back resistant strains, but with no measured results
Hybrids reported with no outbreaks over 6 and 7 years and lower medication costs
findings.practice_en: hybrid mandarin fish breeding and farming

priority.reason: Disease is a large problem and breeding could help, but evidence is two measured studies and mostly farmer reports. Side-by-side farm trials are the missing step, but strain trade-offs are a risk.

action_en: Study whether keeping dissolved oxygen high in intensive mandarin fish culture reduces ISKNV outbreaks and other disease.
action_zh: 研究人员应研究在集约化鳜养殖中保持高溶氧是否能减少传染性脾肾坏死病毒(ISKNV)暴发及其他疾病。
evidence_gap: No claim measures how aeration or oxygen level changes infection or disease in mandarin fish; the hypoxia–ISKNV link comes from a background statement.
risks: Experimental hypoxia or infection challenges can harm the fish used, and the results may not transfer to farm conditions.

basis.reason: These findings share one gap: hypoxia is repeatedly linked to disease outbreaks, yet aeration studies do not report disease outcomes. F0406 and F0601 supply the hypothesis, while F1776 and F1688 show that aeration is widely used but unmeasured for disease. With only one unmeasured claim linking high oxygen to lower disease risk, research is the strongest supported type.

findings.why: Background claim that hypoxia may promote ISKNV replication, with measured physiological stress but no infection data.
Reports unstable oxygen in intensive farming and links hypoxia to outbreaks, without measured disease.
Shows mechanical aeration prevents hypoxic deaths but has no disease effect shown.
One claim links high dissolved oxygen to lower disease risk but gives no figures.

priority.reason: Hypoxia is common in intensive culture and aeration is widely used (26 papers), but the hypoxia and ISKNV link rests on one background claim. It is a research gap with real stakes.

action_en: Check mandarin fish regularly under the microscope and by dissection, sampling about every 7 to 15 days, so parasites such as Trichodina are found early, and record the results.
action_zh: 养殖户应定期（约每7至15天）对鳜鱼进行镜检和解剖抽查，及早发现滴虫等寄生虫，并做好记录。
evidence_gap: Apart from one trial reporting no large outbreaks, no study measures whether routine monitoring lowers parasite burden or mortality.
risks: Netting and sampling fish stresses them, and a missed or late check gives false reassurance, particularly for small fry.

basis.reason: These findings all describe the same practice, regular pond checks with microscopy and sampling, and agree on early detection of parasites, especially Trichodina in small fry. I chose them over general diagnosis findings because they give concrete sampling intervals and methods. Only one trial reports an outcome, so the action is monitoring rather than a stronger recommendation.

findings.why: Describes pond patrols and sampling every 7-10 days with microscopy and dissection.
findings.practice_en: regular health monitoring by sampling and inspection

findings.why: Gives sampling every 10-15 days and notes Trichodina is especially harmful to small fry.
findings.practice_en: health monitoring and early disease detection
findings.practice_zh: 健康监测与早期病害诊断

findings.why: One trial found no large-scale outbreaks and generally high survival with regular microscopy and prompt treatment.
Describes checking body surface and gills every two days and early treatment with approved drugs.

priority.reason: Regular microscopy finds parasites such as Trichodina early and is cheap, with 6+ agreeing papers. No study measures a benefit apart from one trial with no large outbreaks, and sampling stresses fish.

action_en: Test copper sulfate-ferrous sulfate and formalin treatments on mandarin fish fry at small scale, checking dose, mortality and stress before routine use.
action_zh: 研究人员应先小规模试验硫酸铜-硫酸亚铁合剂和福尔马林对鳜鱼苗的处理，在常规使用前核查剂量、死亡率和应激反应。
evidence_gap: Reports conflict on whether 0.7 mg/L copper-ferrous sulfate works or kills fry, and safe dose ranges for fry under farm conditions are not established.
risks: One paper reported mass fry mortality with copper-ferrous sulfate, and formalin dips are reported to cause considerable stress and can kill weak fish.

basis.reason: These findings all cover the same chemicals against parasites in fry, and they disagree: some report good control, while others report failure, stress or mortality. I picked them over the many descriptive drug findings because they contain this conflict. Because of it, the evidence supports careful testing rather than adopting or avoiding the treatments outright.

findings.why: Reports good control of Trichodina with a 5:2 mixture at 0.7 mg/L in a few measured cases.
findings.practice_en: copper sulfate and ferrous sulfate mixture for parasite control
findings.practice_zh: 硫酸铜硫酸亚铁合剂杀虫（治疗车轮虫病）

findings.why: Includes a measured case where 0.7 ppm copper-ferrous sulfate failed and caused mass fry mortality.
Shows formalin baths can work but cause considerable stress and can kill weak fish.
Supports copper sulfate seedling baths as claimed to kill parasites, with few measurements.
findings.practice_en: copper sulfate bath disinfection of fish seedlings

priority.reason: Parasite treatments are widely used and are reported to work, but evidence conflicts: one paper reported mass fry mortality with copper-ferrous sulfate and formalin dips stress fish. Small-scale testing is sensible but the gain is limited.

action_en: Use antimicrobial susceptibility testing on bacterial isolates before choosing antibiotics for mandarin fish, and keep records to monitor resistance.
action_zh: 兽医在为鳜鱼选用抗生素前应对细菌分离株进行药敏试验，并记录数据以监测耐药性。
evidence_gap: No study measures whether choosing drugs by susceptibility testing improves fish disease outcomes or limits resistance on mandarin fish farms.
risks: Antibiotic use can select for resistance, and testing delays treatment and adds cost.

basis.reason: These findings together show that isolates from mandarin fish differ in drug sensitivity, with some resistant strains, and that papers advise resistance monitoring and rational drug use. I did not cite the many findings that simply describe drug treatments as effective, because they give no resistance information. Benefit to disease outcomes is not measured, so the action is limited to monitoring rather than adoption.

findings.why: Measured sensitivity and resistance patterns across antibiotics in mandarin fish isolates.
Notes drug treatment is generally effective but one isolate was resistant, and advises resistance monitoring.
Supports controlled dose, low-toxicity drugs and treatment according to national rules.

priority.reason: Susceptibility testing is measured as a lab method and is sensible practice, but no study shows it improves disease outcomes. It adds delay and cost.

action_en: Researchers should run controlled trials in mandarin fish that compare MS-222, eugenol, 2-phenoxyethanol and ice-water anaesthesia on measured stress and survival during handling and transport.
action_zh: 研究人员应开展对照试验,比较MS-222、丁香酚、2-苯氧乙醇和冰水麻醉对鳜鱼在操作和运输过程中应激指标及存活率的影响。
evidence_gap: None of the findings measured a welfare outcome for any anaesthetic in mandarin fish, so no agent can be shown to reduce handling or transport stress.
risks: Trials add handling and anaesthetic exposure for the fish, and results from sampling doses (e.g. 20–200 mg/L MS-222, 20–40 mg/L eugenol, 150 mg/L 2-phenoxyethanol) may not carry over to transport conditions.

basis.reason: These four findings all describe anaesthetics widely used on mandarin fish at stated doses, with only stated aims of reducing stress and no measured welfare effect. I grouped them because they are alternatives for the same purpose and can be compared side by side. I left out the sampling-only findings, and the evidence is purely descriptive, so only research is supported, not adoption.

findings.why: MS-222 widely used at about 20–200 mg/L, but no welfare outcome measured
Eugenol routine use at 20–40 mg/L, stress reduction only a stated purpose
2-phenoxyethanol at 150 mg/L, stress reduction stated but not measured
Ice-water anaesthesia used, with stress reduction as aim only

priority.reason: Anaesthetic use is very common (77 papers on MS-222) yet no welfare outcome is measured for any agent. The gap is real but the gain is limited to handling and transport, and trials add exposure.

action_en: Researchers should run controlled farm trials of automatic feeders and automated feed-training equipment for mandarin fish, measuring feed-acceptance success, feeding rhythm, appetite-based feeding, and welfare indicators against hand feeding.
action_zh: 研究人员应开展受控的养殖场试验，比较自动投喂机和自动驯食设备与人工投喂对鳜鱼的影响，测量驯食成功率、摄食节律、按食欲投喂的效果及福利指标。
evidence_gap: No measured welfare effects exist for automatic feeding or automated training in mandarin fish; the current claims are speculation or patent descriptions, and the training evidence comes partly from largemouth bass.
risks: Trials cost farm time and equipment, and poorly tuned machines could underfeed or overfeed fish, or stress them during training or grading.

basis.reason: Both findings concern automated feeding-related equipment for the same welfare problem (feeding, including live prey) and both lack any measured results. I grouped them in one research action because the sources only describe or speculate about the devices. The type is research rather than test_on_farms or adopt because there is no measured benefit to build on and no mandarin fish data for one of the claims.

findings.why: Speculates that on-demand, appetite-recognising feeding gives even feeding; feeders could help study feeding rhythms.
Speculates that mimic feeding, precise feeding and grading could raise training success; patent only for largemouth bass fry.

priority.reason: Automation could help feed training, but the claims are speculation or patent descriptions with no measured effects. Trials need equipment, and badly tuned machines could harm fish.

action_en: Research whether strains bred or screened for easy acceptance of dead feed actually have better welfare, by testing health, stress and survival alongside feed uptake.
action_zh: 研究针对易驯食(接受死饵)而选育或筛选的品系是否真正改善福利,在摄食之外同时检测健康、应激和存活。
evidence_gap: No paper measures a welfare outcome of breeding or culling for feed acceptance; they only describe genetic and body-shape differences between accepting and refusing fish, plus stated views.
risks: Culling fish that refuse dead feed may remove fish without improving their welfare, and selection may link feed acceptance to unwanted traits such as poor disease resistance.

basis.reason: These findings share the aim of moving from live prey to formulated feed through breeding or screening. F0639 gives measured differences between groups, but F0641 and F0636 are stated views and F0642 reports mixed results. Because none measures a welfare outcome, I chose research, not adoption.

findings.why: Measured gene and body differences between feed-accepting and refusing fish, with no welfare result
Three papers say easily trained strains are key to leaving live prey, but with no measurements
findings.practice_en: breeding easily trained strains for artificial feed

findings.why: 2011 claims that marker-assisted selection solves problems including disease, with no data
findings.practice_en: domestication and selective breeding for formulated feed acceptance
findings.practice_zh: 驯化选育（人工饲料驯化）

findings.why: Reports most fish still refusing feed after five generations, so the benefit is unproven

priority.reason: Feed-acceptance breeding would reduce live-prey reliance, but no paper measures a welfare outcome, and earlier selection gave sick fish. Research is justified but is long-term.

action_en: Test on farms whether timing prey-fish spawning to match mandarin fish larval first feeding improves first-feeding success and larval survival.
action_zh: 在养殖场试验:使饵料鱼的产卵时间与鳜仔鱼开口摄食相匹配,是否能提高开口成功率和仔鱼成活率。
evidence_gap: Five papers describe the practice but only one has a measurement, and none reports feeding success or survival as a welfare outcome.
risks: Poor timing could leave larvae without suitable food, and keeping prey-fish broodstock adds cost and work.

basis.reason: F0650 is the only finding on supplying suitable live first food and it agrees across five papers. The claims are mostly stated and report no welfare outcome, so I stopped at on-farm testing and did not recommend adoption.

findings.why: Five papers describe synchronising prey spawning with larval first feeding, with little testing
findings.practice_en: synchronized spawning of prey fish for first-feeding live bait
findings.practice_zh: 饵料鱼同步催产(开口饵料同步孵化)

priority.reason: Timing prey-fish spawning for larval first feeding is widely described (5 papers) but only one claim is measured and none shows feeding success or survival. It is niche to hatcheries.

action_en: Test on commercial farms whether routine qPCR viral-load testing every 10-20 days, alongside daily observation, finds infections earlier and improves disease outcomes.
action_zh: 兽医应在商业养殖场测试：每10-20天进行一次qPCR病毒载量检测并结合日常观察，是否能更早发现感染并改善疾病结局。
evidence_gap: No study shows that molecular testing changes disease outcomes or welfare, and the best testing interval and the action thresholds are unknown.
risks: Testing costs money and may need sampling or killing fish, and positive results without a clear response plan may add cost without helping the fish.

basis.reason: The qPCR findings show the method can detect low viral DNA that conventional PCR missed and can confirm MFBV, and one paper recommends testing every 10-20 days. Both are described only as detection tools with no welfare outcome, so I limited this to a farm trial. F0356 is cited because daily health checks are the baseline the testing would be compared with.

findings.why: qPCR detected chronic viral DNA missed by conventional PCR
Pathogen identification and a 10-20 day qPCR monitoring suggestion
Describes the baseline daily checks and early-warning use

priority.reason: qPCR is a measured detection tool, but no study shows that testing improves disease outcomes, and the interval and thresholds are unknown. Cost is high and benefit unclear.

action_en: Trial on farms whether adjusting feed amount and particle size using uneaten-feed collection, belly shape, feeding behaviour and regular sampling reduces underfeeding or wasted feed and improves welfare.
action_zh: 养殖户应在养殖场试验：根据残饵收集、腹部形态、摄食行为和定期抽样结果调整投饵量和饲料粒径，能否减少投饵不足或浪费并改善福利。
evidence_gap: No paper measures a welfare effect of these feed-intake checks, and the methods differ (e.g. 15 vs 30 minutes siphoning, drying temperatures, 10 vs 30 day sampling).
risks: Siphoning, sampling and dissection add labour and stress or kill fish, and appearance-based screening could wrongly label slow-training fish.

basis.reason: These findings describe how intake is judged and how the results are used to adjust feeding, so they fit one feed-adjustment routine. Their strength is only 'described' with no welfare outcomes, so the most I can support is an on-farm trial with standard methods.

findings.why: Describes intake and satiation assessment; may show if feed is sufficient
Describes siphoning and weighing uneaten feed, with inconsistent protocols
Sampling every 10-30 days used to adjust feed amount and particle size
Belly appearance used to identify fish accepting dead feed
findings.practice_en: appearance-based screening of fish feeding acceptance
findings.practice_zh: 外观筛选（腹部饱满度判别驯食效果）

priority.reason: Feed-intake checks are only described, with no welfare effect measured and inconsistent methods. Sampling can stress fish and appearance screening may mislabel fish.

action_en: Monitor antimicrobial resistance in bacteria from mandarin fish farm sites regularly, so that medication decisions can draw on resistance data.
action_zh: 兽医应定期监测鱼场来源细菌的耐药性，使用药决策有耐药数据可依。
evidence_gap: Neither paper measures whether resistance monitoring improves disease control, and no sampling schedule or resistance threshold is given.
risks: Monitoring adds laboratory cost, and results may not lead to better treatment if there is no response plan.

basis.reason: Only this finding addresses resistance, and its two papers recommend or propose resistance monitoring without measured effects. That supports watching an indicator, not a stronger action.

findings.why: Papers recommend regular resistance monitoring and use as a medication indicator

priority.reason: Resistance monitoring rests on two recommendations with no measured effect and no schedule, so its welfare benefit is indirect and unproven.

action_en: Monitor broodfish injury and post-procedure survival wherever artificial insemination is used, and use only skilled, well-coordinated handlers.
action_zh: 凡使用人工授精,应监测亲鱼的损伤和术后存活,并仅由熟练、配合良好的人员操作。
evidence_gap: The two papers give no measurements of injury or survival after artificial insemination, and it is unclear how often it is done properly in practice.
risks: Poorly done handling can stress or injure broodfish and lower their survival, while monitoring adds labour.

basis.reason: F0652 is the only finding on handling during breeding, and both papers warn of stress and injury from improper artificial insemination. The warnings are stated without measurements and the strength is mixed, so I chose monitoring, not a firm avoid or adopt recommendation.

findings.why: States that improper insemination can stress or injure broodfish, lowering survival, and that skilled handlers are needed

priority.reason: Broodfish injury from artificial insemination is stated, not measured, in two papers, and the procedure is little used, so the fish affected are few.

action_en: Researchers should test on farms whether acclimation with anti-stress products and weekly density and disturbance training improves mandarin fish tolerance of tank moves and transport, measuring stress and survival.
action_zh: 研究人员应在养殖场测试抗应激产品驯化以及每周密度和扰动应激训练,是否能提高鳜鱼对换池和运输的耐受性,并测量应激指标和存活率。
evidence_gap: The two papers describe these acclimation practices as supportive but report no measured welfare outcome, so the benefit is unquantified.
risks: Repeated density and disturbance training is itself a stressor and could harm fish if poorly dosed, and anti-stress products add cost.

basis.reason: This is the only finding about preparing fish for handling and transport rather than anaesthetising or killing them. The two papers agree the practices are supportive, but with no measured outcomes the evidence is too thin to recommend adoption, so farm trials are the strongest supported step.

findings.why: Describes anti-stress acclimation and stress training, presented as supportive but unmeasured

priority.reason: Acclimation and stress-training practices are only described in two papers with no measured outcome, and the training itself can stress fish.

action_en: Researchers should study how well the blunt-force head blow, MS-222 followed by decapitation, and MS-222 overdose work as slaughter methods for mandarin fish, measuring time to loss of consciousness and signs of distress.
action_zh: 研究人员应研究头部钝击、MS-222麻醉后断头以及MS-222过量致死作为鳜鱼屠宰方法的效果,测量意识丧失时间和痛苦迹象。
evidence_gap: These methods were only described for killing fish at sampling, with no measured welfare effect and no test of whether they work at farm slaughter scale.
risks: A poorly applied blow or an inadequate anaesthetic dose could leave fish conscious during killing, and sampling methods may not suit commercial volumes.

basis.reason: These findings all describe how mandarin fish were killed at sampling (blunt blow, MS-222 overdose at 75–200 mg/L, MS-222 plus decapitation). I grouped them as candidate kill methods that lack any measured welfare data. Claims that the blow is humane or follows WOAH recommendations are statements, not measurements, so research is the only supported type.

findings.why: Blunt blow to the head used, called humane by one paper but not measured
MS-222 euthanasia at 75–200 mg/L described, no welfare effect reported
MS-222 at 100 mg/L followed by decapitation described only
Sampling euthanasia with MS-222, sometimes with decapitation, described only

priority.reason: Slaughter methods are described only for sampling, with no welfare measurement. Slaughter-method research matters but evidence is nil and trials need an adequate design.

criteria.note: killing is every fish's end, but only if shown to be better

action_en: Research which observable signs and measurable targets should guide monitoring and stop decisions during live mandarin fish transport.
action_zh: 研究人员应研究在活鱼运输中，哪些可观察的征象和可测量的指标应用于指导监测和终止运输的决定。
evidence_gap: No measured welfare outcome exists for transport monitoring, and one paper says precise monitoring and control targets are hard to set.
risks: Without validated targets, farmers may react too late or stop transport unnecessarily, and trials with transported fish may themselves stress them.

basis.reason: This is the only finding on handling and transport, and it is the only one marked mixed. One paper advises watching for floating, head-lifting and drifting, while the other says targets are hard to set, so the evidence is too thin for anything beyond research.

findings.why: Advises watching for floating or drifting fish but notes targets are hard to set

priority.reason: Transport monitoring has only two descriptive claims, one saying targets are hard to set. This is the thinnest evidence and a narrow research question.
